column1: # Query -> the method it should find, against a mastodon checkout.
# DRAFTED BY CLAUDE, NOT YET REVIEWED BY THE OWNER. Every label is a judgement
# about what a person would mean; method behaviour was verified by reading the
# source, not recalled. Queries deliberately avoid naming the method: a query
# containing its own answer measures string matching, which is what
# baseline:name isolates.
# Third Ruby corpus, second app-shaped one: federation, timelines, moderation
# — same bands as the rails and discourse sets so the reports read together.
# Run with:  cd <mastodon checkout> && contour eval <this dir>
# --- easy on purpose: queries that share tokens with the answer's name -------
suspend a misbehaving account
block federation with an entire domain
approve a pending follow request
generate a backup archive of an account's data
recalculate which hashtags are trending
redirect an old permalink to where it now lives
push a new toot into follower home feeds
# --- no token shared with the answer's identifier: the thesis case -----------
look up who an @user@server address belongs to
the timeline you see when you open the app
may this visitor read this post
keep a toot out of a follower's stream when it fails the rules
cap how often one user may repeat an action
notice an instance has been unreachable for days and give up on it
strip markup from a status for previews
the canonical web address of a remote user's profile
does this login look risky
prove an incoming federation message came from its author
# --- behaviour that appears in NO identifier ---------------------------------
# Reconnect-and-retry, subnet masking, per-viewer patching of a shared cache:
# the body knows; no name in the corpus says so.
reopen a dropped connection and try the request once more
make sure two workers never run the same critical section at once
treat a login from the same subnet as one we have already seen
fill viewer-specific fields into a cached toot payload
